plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 3: Polynomial and Rational Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single Cartesian graph showing a rational function together with the two asymptotes it approaches. The horizontal x-axis carries integer ticks from -5 to 5, the vertical y-axis carries even ticks from -12 to 12, and both are tipped with arrowheads. A dashed orange vertical line stands at x = 1 and runs the full height of the frame, labeled x = 1 in orange near its lower end. A dashed teal line of steep positive slope crosses from the lower left to the upper right, labeled Slant asymptote y = 3x + 1 above and right of the origin. The function is a solid dark blue curve in two branches. The left branch enters at the lower left pressed against the teal line, rises to a shallow turning point just below the x-axis near x = 0, then plunges off the bottom of the frame as it nears the orange line. The right branch descends from the top just right of x = 1, turns at a minimum near y = 9, and climbs away to the upper right, again closing on the teal line. Drawing the curve and both dashed lines on one set of axes lets the reader compare each branch against the boundary it hugs. The graph illustrates the case in which the numerator exceeds the denominator in degree by one, so the polynomial quotient supplies a slanted rather than horizontal end behavior.

interactionPlan.concept: A rational function with a numerator degree one higher than its denominator degree will approach a slant asymptote at extreme x-values and a vertical asymptote where the denominator is zero.

teal label 'Slant asymptote y = 3x + 1' right of the y-axis

demo_steps.title: The Rational Curve
demo_steps.narration: A rational function's graph can be complex and split into separate branches. We want to understand what geometric rules govern its overall shape.

demo_steps.title: The Asymptotes
demo_steps.narration: These two dashed lines represent the structural bounds. The vertical line comes from the zero of the denominator; the slant line comes from the polynomial quotient.

demo_steps.title: Combined Behavior
demo_steps.narration: When plotted together, we see that the function's branches are perfectly guided by these two asymptotic boundaries.

demo_steps.title: Local Blow-up (Vertical)
demo_steps.narration: Drag the x-value close to x=1. As the horizontal distance to the vertical asymptote vanishes, the function is forced to spike toward infinity.

demo_steps.title: End Behavior (Slant)
demo_steps.narration: Drag the x-value far from the center. As x grows large, the vertical distance between the curve and the slant asymptote shrinks toward zero, dictating its end behavior.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A vertical asymptote dominates the local behavior where the denominator is zero, while a slant asymptote governs the long-run end behavior as x goes to infinity.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Plot x from -5 to 5, y from -12 to 12. The rational curve is y = 3x + 1 + 2/(x-1). Ensure the orange vertical line x=1 and teal slant line y=3x+1 are dashed and distinctly colored. The interactive probe point should have two thin, possibly dashed guide lines connecting it to both asymptotes (horizontal to x=1, vertical to y=3x+1). Hide the probe and its guide lines when 'Asymptotes only' is selected.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for an x-value probe: the learner drags x along either branch, a point moves on the rational curve, and guide distances to x = 1 and y = 3x + 1 show why the vertical asymptote controls local blow-up while the slant asymptote controls end behavior.

authoredContext:
To find the equation of the slant asymptote, divide 3 x 2 −2x+1 x−1. The quotient is 3x+1, and the remainder is 2. The slant asymptote is the graph of the line g(x)=3x+1. See the figure.

Slant Asymptote when f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0 where degree of p>degree of qby1.

Graph of f(x)=(3x^2-2x+1)/(x-1) with its vertical asymptote at x=1 and a slant asymptote aty=3x+1.

Case 3: If the degree of the denominator = degree of the numerator, there is a horizontal asymptote at y= a n b n, where a n and b n are the leading coefficients of p(x) and q(x) for f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0.
